etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin connectere (“fasten together”), from con- (“together”) +‎ nectere (“bind”), which is cognate with English knot and English knit.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, of an object) To join (to another object): to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to another object.
(intransitive, of two objects) To join: to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to each other.

Both roads have the same name, but they: they're on opposite sides of the river

definitions.definition: (intransitive, of a blow) To arrive at an intended target; to land.
(transitive, of an object) To join (two other objects), or to join (one object) to (another object): to be a link between two objects, thereby attaching them to each other.

definitions.definition: (transitive, of a person) To join (two other objects), or to join (one object) to (another object): to take one object and attach it to another.
To join an electrical or telephone line to a circuit or network.
To associate; to establish a relation between.
To make a travel connection; to switch from one means of transport to another as part of the same trip.
